To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concept of a bioeconomy is highly political; there is considerable disagreement as to what a “good” bioeconomy should look like, and there are diverging narratives about the bioeconomy.

(i) the concept of the “bioeconomy” is highly ambiguous, (ii) it is used as a political instrument for legitimizing diverging techno-political visions of the future, and (iii) these visions are often in stark contrast with each other and with the biophysical realities.

(i) there is no consensus on how the bioeconomy should look like, and (ii) the different visions of the bioeconomies that have been identified so far are not equally compatible with the sustainability of the biosphere.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to understand the concept of the “bioeconomy” and the visions of society that it is associated with.
the techno-political choices that are made in the context of a bioeconomy and their implications for the future of our societies.
the question of what a bioeconomically transformed society might look like and which techno-political choices are implied by different narratives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a transition to a bioeconomy is a transition to a different society.
a “bioeconomy” can be a transition to many different things, depending on which type of society is envisioned.
the concept of the “bioeconomy” is not a coherent concept but rather a contested and contesteding concept.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concept of the Bioeconomy has been used as a political umbrella term for very different visions and strategies.
the bioeconomy can be seen as a contested space for the articulation and negotiation of different techno-political imaginaries.

there is a need for a critical discussion on the techno-political choices embedded in different visions of the bioeconomies, and for the development of a shared vision of the future that would enable a more sustainable and equitable society.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to engage in more open and participatory debates on how the bioeconomy can be designed to serve the public good.
the concept of a bioeconomy is not a neutral one and that it can be used to support very different types of socio-ecological transitions.
